deep_dive.title: Better Nearest Neighbor Graph Indices via (Efficient) LLM-Guided Pruning
deep_dive.abstract: Graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) is widely used for large-scale semantic search. Its indices are constructed primarily based on geometric relationships among embeddings of an input dataset (e.g., documents or images), rather than explicitly optimizing for semantic relevance. However, when using these indices for downstream query retrieval, performance is evaluated based on the semantic relevance of the retrieved results to the query. This creates a fundamental "geometry-semantic" mismatch between how the indices are constructed and how their retrieval results are evaluated. While existing LLM-based reranking methods can partially mitigate this mismatch at query time, they leave this underlying structural problem in the graph unresolved. We therefore propose LLM-Guided Graph Pruning (LGP), a general framework that addresses this mismatch directly by leveraging LLM reasoning to refine an existing ANN graph index itself. LGP identifies structurally "low-value" neighbors of nodes and replaces them with LLM-selected alternatives that provide useful semantic information while retaining desired geometric structures of the original graph, including sparsity and efficient navigability. Experiments on representative semantic retrieval benchmarks show that LGP consistently improves end-to-end retrieval performance over both vanilla greedy graph search and LLM-based reranking across widely used graph-based ANN indices such as DiskANN and HNSW.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Graph-based ANNS indices are built from embedding geometry yet evaluated by semantic relevance, causing a geometry-semantic mismatch; the paper proposes LLM-guided pruning to build better nearest neighbor graph indices.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 图近似最近邻搜索广泛用于大规模语义检索，但其索引主要依据嵌入向量之间的几何关系构建，而检索结果却按语义相关性评估，导致几何与语义之间的错配，现有LLM重排序只能在查询阶段部分缓解。本文提出利用LLM引导的剪枝直接改进近邻图索引的结构，使语义信号融入图构建阶段。实验表明该方法能提升检索结果与查询的语义相关性，同时保持索引构建的高效性。这为图索引构建目标与下游评估目标的对齐提供了新思路。

deep_dive.title: VADER: Filtered Vector Search with Declarative Recall
deep_dive.abstract: Approximate filtered vector search (FVS), a core operation in many data management tasks that combine structured data with vector embeddings, exhibits increased complexity due to the characteristics of filtering predicates. Each predicate is defined by selectivity (i.e., the fraction of vectors that satisfy the predicate) and correlation (i.e., the relationship between the filter and the vector space), which can significantly affect search difficulty even for the same query vector. This poses a key challenge for users aiming to integrate vector search with structured data, as efficient execution often requires extensive manual tuning of algorithm parameters. In this paper, we present VADER, the first approach that eliminates hyperparameter tuning by introducing declarative recall for approximate filtered vector search. With declarative recall, users specify a desired recall target, and VADER executes FVS queries to meet this target without requiring manual configuration. VADER achieves this by employing a filter-aware recall predictor that generalizes across varying selectivities and correlations without explicit tuning, and by performing early termination once the predicted recall reaches the user-defined target. Through extensive experimental evaluation, we show that VADER achieves near-optimal early termination, while providing significant speedups of up to 53% faster and improved result quality of 28% compared to the best-performing baseline.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Approximate filtered vector search combines structured predicates with vector embeddings but needs heavy manual parameter tuning. VADER introduces declarative recall, removing hyperparameter tuning by letting users state target recall while the system adapts search automatically.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 近似过滤式向量搜索是把结构化过滤谓词与向量嵌入结合的核心操作，但谓词的选择性与相关性会显著改变检索难度，用户往往需要手工调参才能高效执行。本文提出VADER，首次通过引入声明式召回率来消除超参数调优，用户只需声明目标召回，系统自动适配搜索策略。该工作直接面向向量数据库检索的效率与召回控制，属于向量检索系统的强相关研究。
